label: Peplink PSW-8-240W-RUG
description: Rugged industrial 8-port PoE+ SD switch with two 1G SFP cages, 240 W PoE budget.
notes: Vendor figures from the Peplink switch datasheet: **8x GE Ports (PoE+), 2x 1G SFP Ports**, 240 W PoE budget. The SFP cages are 1G here, not 10G - this is the rugged access switch, and the SFP+ figures elsewhere in the same datasheet belong to the higher PSW models, which is exactly the confusion that makes row-level verification worth the trouble.

label: Peplink Balance Two
description: Dual-WAN branch router: 2x GE WAN, 4x GE LAN, 1 Gbps routing throughput and 150 Mbps PepVPN.
notes: Vendor figures from the Peplink datasheet: WAN Interface **2x 10/100/1000M Ethernet**, LAN Interface **4x 10/100/1000M Ethernet**, Router Throughput 1 Gbps, PepVPN/SpeedFusion Throughput 150 Mbps. **The VPN figure is the one that matters for a SpeedFusion plan**: 150 Mbps against 1 Gbps of routing throughput means a tunnel is a seventh of the line rate, and a lab built on the routing number will expect six times the encrypted throughput the box can do.

label: Peplink MAX BR1 Mini HW3 (LTE-E)
description: Compact mobile router, HW3, EMEA LTE: 3x GE LAN (one convertible to WAN with PrimeCare), 300 Mbps throughput, Wi-Fi, PoE in.
notes: Vendor figures from the Peplink tech-spec sheet: Ethernet WAN port **0 / 1 (GE)**, Number of Ethernet LAN port **3 / 2 (GE)**, Router Throughput 300 Mbps, Wi-Fi AP Yes, PoE Input Yes, SFP LAN/WAN No. The paired numbers are a licensing effect: with a PrimeCare subscription one LAN port can be turned into a WAN port, giving 1 WAN / 2 LAN instead of 0 WAN / 3 LAN. The base configuration is modelled; **a BR1 Mini with PrimeCare enabled has a different port split from this file.** The **-LTE-E** suffix is the EMEA LTE band set; the ports are identical to the LTEA SKUs, so only the band coverage differs.
